name: Criminal defence files
one_line: The practitioner-side matter file in which the CLIENT IS A NATURAL PERSON ACCUSED BY THE STATE, and in which the practice holds a large body of material ABOUT PEOPLE WHO ARE NOT THE CLIENT - a complainant, a witness, a co-accused, a person never charged - that was SERVED on it by the accusing side and that it is permitted to hold only for these proceedings. It is NOT activated by the practice-area words criminal, defence, prosecution or offence, by a `R v` or `State v` caption, by an offence name, by a police-force or prosecutor name, by a custody or charge reference standing alone, or by a document-type word such as charge sheet, indictment or bail sheet; a practice area is a VALUE of `work_type` and this row concedes that ruling in full, as `law_practice`'s NJ-LP-4 demanded. It survives on LEG THREE ONLY - three privacy rules its schema's default template does not state: (1) a SERVED THIRD-PARTY BUNDLE held under a use restriction, whose subjects are neither the holder nor the client nor the client's counterparty, which may never be copied for convenience, de-duplicated across matters, or synced; (2) SELF-INCRIMINATING CLIENT WORK PRODUCT - a proof of evidence, an advice-on-plea attendance note - whose narrative body may never be excerpted into a preview line, a group label, a snippet or a remote prompt at any confidence, so recognition here runs on labelled slots alone; (3) SENSITIVITY THAT RISES AT CLOSURE rather than decaying, because an acquittal, a discontinuance, a caution or a spent conviction is the most disclosive artefact in the file and it arrives LAST, which inverts every ordinary old-files-are-cold heuristic. Its filing rule differs from the schema default in one further way no sibling states: not only is the client level ineligible, the DOCUMENT-FUNCTION level is constrained too, because a function label naming a plea, a disposal, a conviction history or a psychiatric assessment discloses the accusation even when the client name and the matter reference are opaque.

deterministic: PRECONDITION, INHERITED WHOLE AND NOT CLAIMED AS A DIFFERENCE. The `law_practice` schema default must hold first: an exact matter, file or engagement reference repeated across two or more artefacts, PLUS at least one artefact whose own labelled slots separate a practitioner or firm role from a client role. The schema's deletion test applies here unchanged and is unusually load-bearing in this world, because this world is dense in struck tokens - delete every entity name (a firm, a court, a police force, a prosecutor, two surnames in a caption) and every document-type word (charge sheet, indictment, bail sheet, custody record), and if nothing structural survives, nothing fires. Nothing below is a licence to write a `law_practice` fact; the schema declares no field rows under PR-6.

THE SERVED-SCHEDULE PAIR, and it is this row's one genuinely new detection structure because its DIRECTION is inverted from the schema's own disclosure-review signal. The schema's signal is a review or coding log THE HOLDER AUTHORED - one row per document, the holder's reviewer, the holder's coding decision. This structure is a schedule the holder RECEIVED: one row per item, an item description, a per-item disclosability or undermines/assists decision, and an AUTHOR-ROLE SLOT NAMING AN OFFICER OF THE OPPOSING SIDE (a disclosure officer, a prosecutor), together with a service or date-served endorsement. The holder cannot alter a single row of it. It normally arrives as a PAIR - a schedule of material being served and a schedule of material being withheld or listed as unused - and the holder's own file carries the reciprocal artefact, a further-disclosure request or defence statement responding item by item. It is the pair plus the foreign author role plus the service endorsement that is the signal, never the offence words on it. Provenance: inference.

A DETAINED-PERSON RECORD structure: a timed log of events concerning ONE person's detention - arrival, rights advisement or caution block, review times, an attending legal-adviser slot, an appropriate-adult or interpreter slot, and a release or charge disposition line - carrying a custody or booking reference that is distinct from the matter reference and that recurs on the interview record and the bail sheet. The TIMED-LOG-PLUS-ROLE-SLOTS shape is the signal; a custody reference alone is a struck token. Read through 00's direct-fact path for a labelled form field. Provenance: inference.

A CHARGE-TO-OUTCOME SPINE: two artefacts bearing the same proceeding reference where one carries a numbered list of allegations with a per-count structure (count, allegation, statutory reference slot) and the other carries a per-count DISPOSITION slot with a date. The spine is what makes the file a matter rather than a heap, and its terminal member is the artefact this row's privacy rule protects hardest. The product records the disposition as a LITERAL OBSERVATION and decides no legal status, no guilt, no innocence, no spent-ness and no expungement eligibility. Provenance: inference.
needs_llm: WHICH SIDE THE HOLDER IS ON, which is the schema's standing question and is sharpest here because the same served bundle exists in the accused's own hands, in defence counsel's hands, and in the prosecuting authority's hands. The model reads explicit role slots - who is addressed, who signed, who allocated the reference, who is described as instructed - and abstains rather than inferring a side from a firm name or a folder.

WHETHER A NAMED PERSON IN A DOCUMENT IS THE CLIENT OR A THIRD PARTY, which decides whether this row's use-restriction rule attaches. A previous-convictions schedule and a psychiatric report look identical whether the subject is the accused or a complainant; the discriminating evidence is an addressee, instructing-party or subject slot, and where it is absent the answer is unresolved, not a guess.
WHETHER AN INTERVIEW RECORD IS A DETAINED-PERSON INTERVIEW OR AN INVESTIGATORY INTERVIEW CONDUCTED FOR A CLIENT, read from the role trio present on the page rather than from the word interview.

WHETHER AN ARTEFACT IS THE SERVED COPY OR THE HOLDER'S OWN WORKING COPY of the same document, because they are not duplicates and must not be collapsed. Read from a service endorsement, an exhibit stamp, a page-numbering scheme applied by the serving side, or an annotation layer.

STRUCTURE ONLY, NEVER NARRATIVE. On any artefact this row identifies as client work product, the model may read section headings, role slots and reference lines and must not read, summarise, embed or quote the account itself. This is the operational form of this row's second privacy rule, and it is a recognition constraint, not merely a display one.
never_alone: an `R v`, `State v`, `People v` or `Rex/Regina` caption, or any two-name adversarial caption
an offence name, a statutory section reference, or a sentencing term
a police force, prosecuting authority, court, custody suite or firm name
a custody, booking, charge, URN, docket or arrest reference standing alone
a document-type word: charge sheet, indictment, information, bail sheet, custody record, plea, mitigation, unused material
an accused's, complainant's or witness's personal name, in any position including a filename
a folder named for a case, a client, a court year or a practice area
a confidentiality, restriction or not-for-further-disclosure legend, which is a literal observation and never this product's classification
the practice-area words criminal or defence anywhere, including in an email signature block or a letterhead

proposed_context_terms: initial details of the prosecution case
work_types: charge, indictment or information record and initial prosecution case details
detained-person and interview record, including prepared statements and adviser attendance
served prosecution evidence bundle and its service endorsement
unused-material schedule, further-disclosure request and defence statement
third-party subject material - previous convictions, medical, social-care or school records about a person who is not the client
client proof of evidence and instructions on plea
expert and assessment report obtained for the proceedings, including fitness and pre-sentence material
bail, remand, condition and listing record
hearing preparation, case management and trial note
mitigation, basis of plea and sentencing record
outcome, disposal, discontinuance or acquittal record and the closure file
grouping_reasons: ONE PROSECUTION FROM CHARGE TO OUTCOME, joined by an exact repeated matter or proceeding reference - inherited from the schema default and restated only because this group's terminal member changes the group's own risk. "The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent." The anchor supports candidate membership and copies no party, allegation, disposition, offence or third-party fact onto any member.

ONE SERVICE EVENT: the schedules, the bundle and the covering endorsement that arrived together on one date from the opposing side, joined by the service date and the serving-party slot. This group is bounded deliberately so the use restriction attaches to a set the user can see, and its members must not be merged into the holder's own working copies of the same documents.

ONE DETENTION EPISODE: the custody record, the interview record, the adviser attendance note and the bail or charge disposition, joined by an exact custody or booking reference that is NOT the matter reference. Grouping by this second reference is what lets an episode be recognised before a matter reference exists at all.

ONE THIRD-PARTY SUBJECT, and this is the only group in the family whose purpose is EXCLUSION RATHER THAN RETRIEVAL: the material about one named person who is not the client, gathered so it can be protected and so it never travels with the matter into a preview, a summary, a duplicate scan or a remote prompt. It is grouped in order to be walled off. Its label must not name the person.

A candidate group is bounded by an exact reference and never by a name, a caption, an offence, a court, a date range or semantic similarity - "It should not form a supported group when there is no valid anchor". Two matters concerning the same complainant, the same estate of facts or the same co-accused are NOT one group, and cross-matter similarity is suppressed here rather than merely deprioritised.

template.why: EMPTY BY CONTRACT, AND THEN CONSTRAINED ONE LEVEL DEEPER THAN ANY SIBLING - which is this row's leg-three difference stated as a filing rule. By contract there is nothing to order: `law_practice` declares no field rows under PR-6, a dimension may only branch on a field the same schema declares, and this template mints nothing. The measurable comparison is therefore against the schema default's PROSE recommendation - the client only where the corpus spans more than one AND the user has explicitly approved a client-named branch, then the matter, then the document function, then the period. THIS ROW DIFFERS AT TWO LEVELS, NOT ONE. (1) THE CLIENT LEVEL IS INELIGIBLE OUTRIGHT AND NOT UNLOCKABLE. In the default the client is typically a company and the disclosure is commercial; here a client-named branch writes into the filesystem that a named natural person stands accused of a crime, which is a statement about their liberty that no folder should make, against "The default posture must therefore be local-first and data-minimizing." `law_practice.family-law` reached the same absolute for its own reason; this row reaches it for a different one and both should survive R1c or neither should. (2) THE FUNCTION LEVEL IS ALSO CONSTRAINED, AND NO OTHER TEMPLATE IN THE FAMILY SAYS THIS. Suppressing the client name and opacifying the matter reference is not sufficient here, because the schema's third level - document function - is itself disclosive in this world: `mitigation`, `basis of plea`, `previous convictions`, `pre-sentence report`, `fitness to plead` each publish the accusation, the client's history or their mental health from the branch label alone, with no name anywhere in the path. Function labels that name a plea, a disposal, a conviction history or a clinical assessment are therefore ineligible as folder levels even when every other level has been redacted. (3) A NAMED THIRD PARTY may never be a level at all, inherited from the schema and reinforced: a complainant, a witness, a co-accused or a person never charged is the strongest case in the whole family, because a path writes their identity into a filesystem that every later process reads. NOT TIME-FIRST: "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." Charge date, service date, hearing date, document date and filesystem time mean different things here, nothing is capture-based, and a year-first tree would additionally scatter one prosecution across the calendar boundary that its own outcome usually crosses. Whatever lands stays a recommendation the user may reverse, remove, add to or flatten.

collides_with.signal: SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Bail conditions and PTPH listing - 41127-0011.ics` beside the covering letter and charge sheet that arrive with it. THE ACCUSED HOLDS THE SAME DOCUMENTS AS THEIR OWN DEFENCE PRACTICE DOES. Toward that neighbour: the holder IS the accused, keeping their own charge sheet, bail sheet, solicitor's letters and outcome record about their own liberty; every token this row looks for is present except the apparatus. Toward this row: the practice ALLOCATED the reference, produced the attendance notes and the proof of evidence, RECEIVED the served bundle under a use restriction, and recorded time - and the accused is somebody else. THE DECIDING EVIDENCE IS WHERE THE APPARATUS IS, never the caption, never the offence, never the practice-area word, never the folder. The cost asymmetry is stated so R1c can weigh it: a personal file misrouted here is over-classification into a protective home, while a client's file misrouted there mixes a third party's accusation into the holder's own life and strips the use restriction from a served bundle - so where the side is unresolved the answer is Review Later, not a guess in either direction.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Unused material schedule - served 2026-05-12 - 41127-0011.pdf` beside a civil disclosure review log - both are a one-row-per-document table with a per-item decision column, an officer name and a date. Toward that neighbour: the log is the HOLDER'S OWN, its reviewer is the holder's fee-earner, its coding decisions are the holder's to make and change, and it is produced in order to disclose outward. Toward this row: the schedule was AUTHORED BY THE OPPOSING SIDE'S OFFICER AND SERVED INWARD, the holder cannot alter a row of it, and the material it lists is held under a use restriction and may not be copied or de-duplicated across matters. Discriminated by the AUTHOR-ROLE SLOT ON THE LOG plus a service endorsement, never by the offence words or the practice area. The reciprocal is owed: that row should say that a review log whose decision column belongs to a foreign officer is not its evidence.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES, AND THIS IS THE RECIPROCAL THAT ROW EXPLICITLY ASKED FOR AS NJ-FL-2: `Non-molestation order and statement of complainant - withheld address.pdf`. One order, two matters. Toward that neighbour: the order was obtained IN the family proceedings, the file is the applicant's protection application, the subjects are two members of one household and often a child, and the withheld-address slot protects one named person from the other named person inside the same file. Toward this row: the SAME order becomes served prosecution evidence in a prosecution FOR ITS BREACH, the client is the ACCUSED - the respondent to the order, the person the withheld address is withheld FROM - and the discriminating slots are a charge or count structure plus an accused-role slot plus a custody or bail record. BOTH sides carry a withheld-address slot, which is why this pair answers NJ-FL-2: the two rows do NOT hold the same privacy rule. That row's rule is an internal boundary between two people who are both its subjects; this row's is a use-restricted bundle about people who are not its subject at all, held by the practice acting for the person they are protected from. The rules point in opposite directions and neither collapses into the other.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Interview transcript - 2026-03-04 - Rowan Pike.pdf`. Both rows hold a dated question-and-answer record of one person being questioned inside a practitioner matter, on the practice's template, with the matter reference in the footer. Toward that neighbour: an investigation CONDUCTED FOR a client - the practice is the questioner, the subject is a third party being examined, and the anchor is an investigation instruction or engagement reference. Toward this row: an interview in which the practice's CLIENT IS THE ONE BEING QUESTIONED BY THE STATE, and the practice attends as adviser - the discriminating slots are a caution or rights-advisement block, an attending-legal-adviser role slot, and a custody or booking reference distinct from the matter reference. The seam is the DIRECTION OF QUESTIONING read off the role slots, never the word interview and never the offence vocabulary.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Psychiatric report - fitness to plead - re client - 41127-0011.pdf`, and the complainant's medical records obtained by third-party application that sit beside it. Toward medical: a clinical assessment of a named person is medical's own evidence on its own structure, medical is a safety domain and ITS PROTECTION RUNS FIRST - this row takes nothing away from that and co-activation is the correct outcome. Toward this row: the SAME bytes carry an INSTRUCTING-PARTY slot naming the practice and an ADDRESSEE slot naming a court, plus a matter reference, which makes them a member of the prosecution's group. The consequence is asymmetric and must be stated: medical's own facts - `provider`, `record_type` - must stay UNKNOWN here, because medical's records are the HOLDER's and this subject is a third party who did not choose this filesystem, and this row's use restriction must not be lost merely because a medical protection also attached. Discriminated by the instruction letter and the addressee slot, never by the clinical vocabulary.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES, AND IT IS THE FAMILY'S ORTHOGONALITY SEAM RATHER THAN A TRUE MUTEX: `Exhibit RP1 - CCTV - Station Rd 2026-02-11.mp4` and the index that binds it. Toward that neighbour: it owns the INDEX-TO-ITEM BINDING as a structure - an exhibit index, an exhibit reference scheme, a bundle pagination - in any matter of any kind, and that is a document-function claim. Toward this row: the same items when they arrive as SERVED material with a service endorsement, a foreign numbering scheme and a use restriction, and whose subjects are complainants and witnesses. The discriminating evidence is the SERVICE ENDORSEMENT AND SERVING-PARTY SLOT, never the media type and never the exhibit numbering. RECOMMENDATION FOR R1c, RECORDED HERE AND NOT ACTED ON: the practice-area rows and the document-function rows on this schema are ORTHOGONAL AXES, and a criminal exhibit bundle plausibly wants both rows rather than a winner. If R1c rules that a file may hold a function row and a practice-area row simultaneously, this entry should become a co-activation note rather than a collision; `also_holds_with` is schema-to-schema only under CONNECTION section 5, so a template cannot record that intent as an edge and this row does not try.

falls_through_to.why: Named first and it takes nearly everything this row recognises whenever the matter cannot be confidently anchored, because the characteristic isolated file here is a document about a named natural person's accusation or about a third party who is not the client at all. 00 names this residual and licenses exactly this behaviour: "Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts." The last clause is why this residual and not another: a criminal-defence filename frequently carries the accusation, so a residual that suppresses filenames from prompts is the only correct home for an orphan here.

The home for this family's defining failure and this row's sharpest one: a real-looking criminal document whose SIDE or whose SUBJECT ROLE is unresolved - practitioner or accused, client or complainant. The collision fixtures route here by design rather than by accident, because guessing either way has a real cost and abstention has almost none.

Encrypted archives, malformed served bundles, proprietary case-management binaries and unreadable media exports are frequent here and must be represented without forced inspection. A filename carrying a court word and a year manufactures no matter, no subject and no sensitivity result.

Public judgments, sentencing guidelines, practitioner texts and precedent copies are dense in this row's struck tokens and belong here absent an exact accepted matter or research reference. Routing them here is what keeps criminal vocabulary from becoming an activation signal.

A positively evidenced screen capture of a court portal or listing whose OCR does not establish an accepted matter belongs here rather than in a protected matter group, since a capture is the weakest possible anchor for a group whose members carry a use restriction.

sensitivity_why: The strictest posture available, and this row does not merely inherit it - THIS IS THE LEG OF THE NODE TEST THE ROW STANDS ON, because its schema ruled that a practice-area row survives only if it changes the privacy rule and never because it changes the topic. Three changes, none of which the `law_practice` default states, and none of which duplicates `law_practice.family-law`. FIRST, A USE-RESTRICTED BUNDLE ABOUT NON-SUBJECTS. The schema's posture protects a third party the practice acts FOR. Here the practice additionally holds a large body of material about people it acts AGAINST or who are merely caught up - a complainant, a witness, a co-accused, a person never charged - served on it by the accusing side and permitted to be held for these proceedings only. 00's corpus sentence describes this pile exactly: a real collection "can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records", and here every one of those may be about somebody who is not the client and not the holder. The operational rules that follow are new: this material may never be copied for convenience, never de-duplicated or version-merged against an identical schedule in another matter, never synced, and the SERVED copy and the holder's own working copy are not duplicates. SECOND, SELF-INCRIMINATING CLIENT WORK PRODUCT, WHICH CONSTRAINS RECOGNITION AND NOT ONLY DISPLAY. A proof of evidence or an advice-on-plea note may record an admission by a living person whose liberty is at stake. The schema's default permits recognition on a minimum-necessary excerpt; this row does not. On those artefacts the product reads heading blocks, section labels and reference lines and NEVER the narrative body - no embedding, no summary, no preview line, no group label, no snippet, no remote prompt, at any confidence - which is the operational form of "The default posture must therefore be local-first and data-minimizing." THIRD, SENSITIVITY RISES AT CLOSURE. Everywhere else in this family a closed matter cools and becomes archivable; here the outcome record - a discontinuance, an acquittal, a caution, a disposal that may later be spent or expunged - is the single most disclosive artefact and it arrives LAST. Every ordinary old-files-are-cold heuristic is therefore inverted for this row, and an old encrypted crown court archive is high-risk precisely because it is old. Two consequences bind all three: nothing here is legally interpreted - no guilt, innocence, admissibility, disclosability, spent-ness, expungement eligibility, bail compliance or breach is decided by this product, and every disposal, restriction endorsement and disclosability column stays a LITERAL OBSERVATION - and no name, address, allegation, account, exhibit content or disposition is placed in a remote prompt by default. Handling classes are P7's and this row assigns none.
open_question: Four. (1) NJ-CD-1, THE PRACTICE-AREA CHARGE, answered as a NARROW YES on leg three exactly as NJ-LP-4 demanded, and recorded so it can be reversed: this row does NOT stand on holding criminal-shaped documents - every one of them is already a `work_type` value on the anchor - it stands on three privacy rules the schema's default does not state (a served use-restricted bundle about non-subjects, a narrative-never-read rule on client work product, and sensitivity that rises at closure) plus one detection structure the default cannot see (a served schedule PAIR whose decision column belongs to a foreign officer, which is the photographic inverse of the schema's own disclosure-review signal). If R1c judges that the use-restriction and non-subject rules belong on the `law_practice` SCHEMA rather than on one template - defensible, since `law_practice.investigation`, `law_practice.discovery` and `law_practice.immigration-casework` can each hold third-party material under a restriction - then the correct outcome is REFUSAL of this row, the rules move up to the schema, and coverage routes to the schema default plus Protected Records. This row would rather be refused than kept for its topic. (2) NJ-CD-2, ANSWERING NJ-FL-2: `law_practice.family-law` asked whether the three allowed practice-area rows carry one privacy rule or three, and asked this row specifically whether a protected-witness-address slot is its rule or the schema's. Answer: the withheld-address slot is THE SCHEMA'S and should move up - it appears in family, criminal and investigation material alike and no row should own it. But the three rows' rules are NOT one: family-law's is an internal boundary between two people who are both its subjects, this row's is a restriction on material about people who are not its subject at all, and the two point in opposite directions on the same protective order. R1c should move the address slot to the anchor and keep the rows distinct, OR merge all three into a protected-natural-persons template with the practice areas as `work_type` values - but it should not do half of each. (3) NJ-CD-3, THE ORTHOGONALITY PROBLEM, and it is bigger than this row: the 36 templates on this schema mix a DOCUMENT-FUNCTION axis (pleadings, discovery, evidence-exhibits, hearing-transcripts, court-filing-record) with a PRACTICE-AREA axis (this row, family-law, immigration-casework). A criminal exhibit bundle sits on both. Alternatives: (a) rule that one file may activate one function row and one practice-area row, in which case this row's `law_practice.evidence-exhibits` and `law_practice.discovery` collisions become co-activation notes; (b) rule the axes mutually exclusive and force a winner per file, which this row believes loses the use restriction; (c) collapse the function rows into `work_type` values, leaving the practice-area rows to carry the privacy differences. `also_holds_with` is schema-to-schema only under CONNECTION section 5, so no template can express (a) as an edge and R1c must settle it. (4) NJ-CD-4, THE FIELD DEPENDENCY: this row's non-subject rule is currently a prohibition with no key behind it. It ENDORSES the anchor's existing `subject_of_record` proposal and mints nothing, and asks that destination-ineligibility live on the KEY rather than being restated by every template. It adds one observation the other proposers cannot: this row needs `subject_of_record` to distinguish a subject who is the CLIENT from a subject who is an ADVERSE THIRD PARTY within a single matter, which is a distinction no other proposer has raised and which decides whether the use restriction attaches.
